episode.title: Publish the prebuilt CLI bundle with platform-specific optional dependencies
episode.before: At parent commit 55db3c776c86798938ccf386f53b1d5593c37468, the release action built the workspace packages and generated the root bundle, but the public npm CLI publish path did not stage that bundle inside packages/cli or rewrite the CLI manifest for a self-contained bundled artifact. packages/cli/package.json still published files from dist, pointed the gemini executable and main entry to dist/index.js, and retained workspace/runtime dependencies, development dependencies, scripts, and release-time configuration.
episode.after: At a5fd5d0b9fcafcc2eb1cc92e8e6405716dbb103f, non-GitHub npm releases run a preparation script after bundle generation and before CLI publication. The script requires the root bundle directory, replaces packages/cli/bundle with its contents, changes the package allowlist and executable entry to bundle/ and bundle/gemini.js, removes dependency, development, script, main, and configuration fields made unnecessary or unsuitable by bundling, and copies the root platform-sensitive optional dependencies into the published CLI manifest while defensively excluding the development-only bundle tool.
episode.diff: The commit adds scripts/prepare-npm-release.js and a seven-line conditional invocation in .github/actions/publish-release/action.yml. The new 67-line script performs a fail-fast bundle precondition check, replaces the package-local bundle directory, and transforms packages/cli/package.json into the manifest for a bundled npm CLI. No test file was added or changed; validation evidence is limited to the script's explicit failure path, the release action's ordering and registry condition, and the resulting manifest transformation encoded by the implementation.

evidence_units.claim: Commit a5fd5d0b9fcafcc2eb1cc92e8e6405716dbb103f has parent 55db3c776c86798938ccf386f53b1d5593c37468, is titled "feat(release): ship esbuild bundle in npm package (#19171)", and changes only .github/actions/publish-release/action.yml and scripts/prepare-npm-release.js with 74 insertions.
evidence_units.source: git show --stat --format=fuller a5fd5d0b9fcafcc2eb1cc92e8e6405716dbb103f; issue-bundle.json linked pull request 19171

evidence_units.claim: In the parent state, packages/cli/package.json allowed only dist, mapped gemini and main to dist/index.js, and contained runtime dependencies, devDependencies, scripts, and config.
The release action already runs `npm run bundle` before package publication, establishing the root bundle as an input available to the newly added preparation step.
The root manifest supplies optional native packages for multiple operating-system and architecture variants, including Darwin, Linux, and Windows node-pty packages, plus keytar and node-pty.

The preparation script resolves bundle at the release working directory, fails with exit status 1 when it is absent, otherwise removes any prior packages/cli/bundle and recursively copies the generated bundle into that package directory.

The preparation script clones root optionalDependencies, removes gemini-cli-devtools defensively, changes the CLI package files allowlist to bundle/, maps the gemini executable to bundle/gemini.js, deletes dependencies, devDependencies, scripts, main, and config, then assigns the filtered optional dependencies and writes the manifest.
The release action invokes the preparation script after core installation and before the CLI token and `npm publish` steps, only when the target registry is not GitHub Packages.
The implementation provides a local precondition oracle: preparation cannot continue without a generated root bundle and emits an instruction to run `npm run bundle` before exiting unsuccessfully.

The release pipeline's existing CLI publication command supports dry-run mode and consumes the package only after the manifest and bundle preparation step, providing the nearest encoded packaging-level validation point, although the evidence bundle contains no status-check result.

No test or specification file changed in the pinned commit, and the supplied bundle explicitly records `no_test_file_change_observed`; therefore no automated regression oracle specific to the new preparation script is established by this episode.
evidence_units.source: git diff --name-only a5fd5d0b^ a5fd5d0b; issue-bundle.json manifest_metadata.provenance.verification

candidate_atomics.name: require-and-stage-generated-release-bundle
candidate_atomics.title: Require and stage the generated release bundle
candidate_atomics.description: Fail before packaging when the generated artifact is missing; otherwise replace the package-local artifact directory with the freshly generated bundle so publication consumes the intended build output.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure the publishable package contains the freshly generated executable bundle and never silently publishes without it.
semantic_action.pre_state: The release build is expected to have produced a root bundle, while the package-local bundle may be absent or stale.
semantic_action.post_state: The package-local bundle is a recursive copy of the generated root bundle, or preparation has stopped with a nonzero exit before publication.
semantic_action.validation: Assert that a missing source bundle exits with status 1; for a present bundle, verify the destination was replaced and contains the generated executable artifact.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-package-manifest-for-bundled-runtime
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile the package manifest with a bundled runtime
candidate_atomics.description: Convert a source-oriented workspace package manifest into a bundle-oriented publication contract while preserving runtime-selected platform support through filtered optional dependencies.

semantic_action.intent: Make the published package execute the bundled entry point without shipping source-build dependency metadata, while retaining optional native packages selected by the install platform.
semantic_action.pre_state: The package manifest targets compiled source output, exposes workspace/runtime and development metadata, and does not declare the generated bundle as its published executable.
semantic_action.post_state: The manifest publishes only the bundle directory, maps the executable to the bundled entry, omits fields superseded by bundling, and carries filtered root optional dependencies for supported platforms.
semantic_action.validation: Read the transformed manifest and verify the files and executable fields target the bundle, removed fields are absent, and optional dependencies equal the root optional set minus explicitly excluded development-only entries.

candidate_atomics.name: gate-bundled-preparation-by-publication-target
candidate_atomics.title: Gate bundled preparation by publication target
candidate_atomics.description: Insert bundle staging and manifest reconciliation immediately before CLI publication for the registry path that consumes the bundled npm layout, without changing the distinct GitHub Packages preparation path.

semantic_action.intent: Apply the bundled package layout only to publication targets whose release contract expects it.
semantic_action.pre_state: The release workflow has generated the bundle and may publish through registry-specific preparation paths, but the public npm path does not yet invoke bundled-package preparation.
semantic_action.post_state: Eligible registry releases prepare the bundled CLI before authentication and publication, while the excluded registry retains its separate preparation behavior.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the workflow condition and ordering, then run the eligible path in dry-run mode to confirm preparation precedes the package publication command; confirm the excluded registry skips this step.

candidate_workflows.name: package-prebuilt-cli-with-cross-platform-optionals
candidate_workflows.title: Package a prebuilt CLI without losing platform-specific runtime support
candidate_workflows.description: A release workflow for staging a generated executable bundle, aligning the package manifest with that bundle, preserving install-time optional native variants, and applying the transformation only to the intended publication target.

workflow_graph.goal: Publish a self-contained prebuilt CLI bundle whose executable and package contents agree with the manifest and whose optional native dependencies remain selectable across supported platforms.
when_to_use: A release pipeline already generates a bundled executable, but the package manifest and files allowlist still describe source-oriented or separately compiled output.
The package needs optional native dependencies selected by operating system or architecture even though ordinary runtime dependencies are absorbed into the bundle.
Different publication targets require distinct package preparation behavior.
anti_goals: Do not redesign the bundler or change the runtime behavior of the generated executable.
Do not remove platform-specific optional dependencies merely because ordinary dependencies are bundled.
Do not apply the bundled manifest transformation to registry paths with a separate packaging contract.
Do not treat successful bundle generation alone as proof that the final package tarball is complete.
not_applicable_when: The published package intentionally ships source or compiled module trees and expects consumers to install its ordinary dependency graph.
No prebuilt bundle is generated before publication.
All publication targets share an identical package-layout contract and no target-specific gate is needed.
Platform-specific components are embedded in the bundle and the package has no install-time optional dependency contract.
inputs: generated bundle directory and expected executable
CLI package name and dry-run publication command
workflow_graph.entry_state: The release pipeline can generate a root executable bundle, but the CLI package still describes dist-based contents and dependencies, and the public registry path has no bundle-specific preparation immediately before publication.
workflow_graph.exit_state: For each eligible publication, the fresh bundle is staged in the package, the package manifest exposes only the bundled executable plus filtered cross-platform optional dependencies, and preparation completes before the CLI publication command; missing bundle input halts publication.

steps.condition: The release target uses the bundled-package contract and bundle generation has been scheduled.
steps.validation: The source bundle must exist; absence exits nonzero, while presence replaces the package-local bundle with the generated artifact tree.

steps.condition: Bundle staging succeeded and the publishable package manifest is readable.
steps.validation: The package allowlist and executable point to the bundle, obsolete source-build fields are absent, and filtered root optional dependencies are present.

steps.condition: The release workflow supports more than one registry packaging contract.
steps.validation: The eligible registry path invokes preparation before CLI publication, and the excluded registry path skips it; use publication dry-run as the encoded package-level check.

validation_ladder: Precondition: verify the generated bundle directory exists and contains the expected executable before mutating the package.
Filesystem: verify the previous package-local bundle is replaced by the generated artifact tree.
Manifest: verify files and bin resolve to the staged bundle; verify bundled-away fields are absent; compare optional dependencies with the authoritative root set after exclusions.
Pipeline: verify the transformation is conditionally ordered after bundle generation and before CLI publication.

Package: execute the existing npm publication dry-run for the eligible registry path and inspect the packed artifact; this is recommended by the workflow contract but no successful run is present in the supplied evidence.

Regression: add isolated tests for missing-bundle failure, stale-destination replacement, manifest rewriting, optional-dependency filtering, and registry gating; these tests are deferred because the pinned change added none.
stop_conditions: Stop before manifest mutation and publication if the generated bundle is missing.
Stop if the expected bundled executable is absent after staging.
Stop if the transformed manifest still points outside the published files allowlist.
Stop if required platform-specific optional dependencies are lost or development-only exclusions remain.
Do not apply this workflow to a publication target whose packaging contract requires the original manifest layout.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle lacks PR discussion, reviews, status checks, and issue body, so the motivating production failure and successful CI results cannot be independently established.
No automated test specific to the preparation script or registry condition was added in the pinned change.
The pinned evidence does not include an inspected npm pack tarball or a recorded successful dry-run, so final artifact completeness is not directly proven.
The development-only exclusion is defensive at the pinned state: the inspected root optionalDependencies list does not contain gemini-cli-devtools, although the script explicitly removes it.

unresolved_questions: Did CI or a release dry-run inspect the resulting npm tarball and execute bundle/gemini.js on each supported operating-system and architecture variant? The supplied GitHub bundle has no status-check or review metadata.
Should the preparation script receive direct automated coverage for failure atomicity and manifest preservation beyond the explicitly removed fields?

Is destructive in-place mutation of packages/cli/package.json acceptable for all release retries, or should release preparation operate on a disposable staging tree? The pinned change does not document that lifecycle contract.
